verses.text: Don’t rebuke an older man, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers;
the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.
Honor widows who are widows indeed.
But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety towards their own family, and to repay their parents, for this is  acceptable in the sight of God.
Now she who is a widow indeed, and desolate, has her hope set on God, and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.
But she who gives herself to pleasure is dead while she lives.
Also command these things, that they may be without reproach.
But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let no one be enrolled as a widow under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man,

being approved by good works, if she has brought up children, if she has been hospitable to strangers, if she has washed the saints’ feet, if she has relieved the afflicted, and if she has diligently followed every good work.
But refuse younger widows, for when they have grown wanton against Christ, they desire to marry;
having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.
Besides, they also learn to be idle, going about from house to house. Not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which they ought not.
I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary for insulting.
For already some have turned aside after Satan.
If any man or woman who believes has widows, let them relieve them, and don’t let the assembly be burdened; that it might relieve those who are widows indeed.
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
For the Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle the ox when it treads out the grain.”  And, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”
Don’t receive an accusation against an elder, except at the word of two or three witnesses.
Those who sin, reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.
I command you in the sight of God, and Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
Lay hands hastily on no one, neither be a participant in other men’s sins. Keep yourself pure.
Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities.
Some men’s sins are evident, preceding them to judgment, and some also follow later.
In the same way also there are good works that are obvious, and those that are otherwise can’t be hidden.

footnotes.content: Correct with respect. Treat older men as fathers, younger as brothers. The church is family — even when correction is needed, love must lead the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Older women as mothers, younger as sisters, in all purity. God calls us to see each other as family. That changes how we speak and how we care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Honor widows who are widows indeed — those with no one else. In a world that forgets the vulnerable, the church must remember. God never forgets them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Families should care for their own first. Gratitude to parents is worship. Taking care of elderly loved ones is not a burden — it's a way to honor God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The widow who has no one puts her hope in God and prays night and day. God sees her. He is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows. He hears every prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A life lived only for pleasure is dead while it lives. True life is found in loving God and others. The things the world chases leave us empty; Jesus satisfies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Command these things so the church is above reproach. Our care for the weak speaks volumes to a watching world. Love is our witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Providing for our own household is part of our faith. It's not about perfection, it's about faithfulness. God cares about how we love those closest to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The church had limited resources, so they cared for widows with proven faithfulness. Wisdom balances mercy and responsibility. Both matter to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A life of good works speaks for itself — raising children, showing hospitality, serving saints, caring for the afflicted. Faithfulness in hidden acts of love doesn't go unnoticed by God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Younger widows were encouraged to marry and build homes. Paul isn't restricting them, he's protecting them and freeing the church to care for those with no other support. Love looks for the wisest way to help.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Breaking a pledge can carry consequences. Our word matters. God takes our commitments seriously, and he calls us to do the same.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Idleness can lead us down a dangerous path. Busy hands serving others keep us from becoming busybodies. The best cure for gossip is to find someone to help.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul encourages younger widows to marry, bear children, and manage their homes. There's dignity in ordinary faithfulness. God is glorified in faithfulness at home as much as anywhere else.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some had already turned away. It's a sober reminder to guard our hearts. We need each other to stay near Jesus when temptation pulls us away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If believers have widows, they should care for them. The church carries the load together, but families have a first responsibility. Shared love bears burdens well.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elders who lead well deserve double honor, especially those who preach and teach. Shepherding is hard work. It's right to appreciate and care for those who feed us God's word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul quotes Deuteronomy 25:4 and Luke 10:7 together, treating both as Scripture. The worker deserves wages — ministry labor has real value. God cares that his servants are cared for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Protect leaders from hasty accusations, but don't cover sin. Two or three witnesses bring fairness and protection for all. Justice and mercy must walk together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sin in leadership must be dealt with publicly when needed, to warn others. Love doesn't ignore sin — it confronts it for the sake of restoration and protection. The goal is always repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul charges Timothy before God, Christ Jesus, and the elect angels — this matters. No prejudice, no partiality. God's standards of justice are higher than ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't lay hands hastily on anyone. Impatience can share in someone else's sins. Keep yourself pure. Wise discernment is an act of love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul gives practical medical advice for Timothy's stomach. God cares about our bodies too. Even apostolic ministry includes taking care of our physical health.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some sins are obvious now, others come to light later. God will bring everything to judgment in his time. We don't need to play judge — we can trust the true Judge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Good works may be hidden now, but they won't stay hidden. God sees every cup of cold water given in Jesus' name. Nothing done for him is forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
